title: Grade 7 Science — Thu, Jun 12
description: Fibre to Fabric — Day 4 of 5: Wool — from sheep to fabric
subject: science

questions.question: The process of cutting the thick fleece from a sheep is called:
questions.explanation: Shearing is the removal of a sheep's wool coat using electric clippers. It is done once or twice a year.

questions.question: After shearing, the wool is washed to remove dust, grease, and dirt. This process is called:
questions.explanation: Scouring is the washing of raw wool with detergent and water to remove grease (lanolin), sweat, and dirt.

questions.question: After scouring, wool fibres are untangled and arranged into thin parallel layers. This is:
questions.explanation: Carding combs out tangles in cleaned wool and arranges fibres parallel to each other before spinning.

questions.question: After carding, the fibres are twisted into yarn by:
questions.explanation: Carded wool is spun — twisted into continuous yarn (thread) that can be woven or knitted into fabric.

questions.question: The correct order of processing wool from sheep is:
questions.explanation: The correct order is: Shear (cut fleece) → Scour (wash) → Card (comb) → Spin (twist into yarn) → Weave (make fabric).

questions.question: Wool is a protein fibre. The protein found in wool is called:
questions.explanation: Wool is made of keratin, the same protein found in human hair and nails. It gives wool its strength and elasticity.

questions.question: Which breed of sheep is famous for producing very fine, soft wool?
questions.explanation: Merino sheep, originally from Spain and now in Australia, produce the finest, softest wool used in premium garments.

questions.question: Pashmina wool comes from:
options: Cashmere goat of Himalayan regions (Ladakh, Kashmir)
questions.explanation: Pashmina (cashmere) is luxurious wool from the soft undercoat of the Changthangi goat found in Ladakh and Kashmir.

questions.question: The 'sorter' in a wool factory:
options: Sorts wool by fibre quality, length, and grade
questions.explanation: Wool sorters grade and separate the fleece by fibre length, fineness, and quality for different textile uses.

questions.question: Sheep wool has a natural oil called ____ which is used in creams and cosmetics.
questions.explanation: Lanolin is a natural waxy oil from sheep's wool. After scouring, it is recovered and used in skin creams and lotions.

questions.question: Wool feels warm because:
options: Crimped wool fibres trap air, creating an insulating layer
questions.explanation: Wool fibres are naturally curly (crimped), trapping millions of tiny air pockets that insulate the body from cold.

questions.question: Which Indian state is a major producer of wool and famous for Pashmina shawls?
questions.explanation: Jammu & Kashmir, particularly Ladakh and the Kashmir valley, is famous for Pashmina (cashmere) shawls.

questions.question: Angora wool comes from:
options: Angora goat (giving mohair) or Angora rabbit (giving angora fibre)
questions.explanation: Angora fibre comes from the Angora rabbit — extremely soft and fluffy. Mohair comes from the Angora goat.

questions.question: One reason wool garments should NOT be washed in hot water is:
options: Hot water makes wool more colourful
Hot water causes wool fibres to shrink and felt (mat together permanently)
questions.explanation: Wool fibres have scales that lock together when agitated in hot water, causing irreversible shrinking and felting.

questions.question: The approximate amount of wool a Merino sheep produces per year is:
questions.explanation: A Merino sheep produces about 3–5 kg of clean wool per year. Some high-quality rams can produce up to 10 kg.
